extracted.intended_audience: American Heart Association grant applicants and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing the American Heart Association's peer-review practices and review criteria used to evaluate biomedical research grant applications in cardiovascular/stroke research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score scale (1-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1-9 scale (1 = exceptional, 9 = poor). Mirrors NIH approach and allows decimals for finer ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric scoring uses a 1 (best) to 9 (worst) scale; reviewers may use decimal values to provide finer discrimination among applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Triage
rubrics_metrics.description: AHA reserves the right to triage at least half of submissions, removing applications unlikely to compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triage reduces reviewer burden by filtering out proposals judged unlikely to be competitive prior to full review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2: Scientific Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Three expert reviewers assigned per non-triaged application, each conducting in-depth review of ~6–9 proposals and preparing written critiques with strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers generate preliminary numeric scores and written critiques identifying strengths and weaknesses; workload targets (6–9 proposals/reviewer) are specified to ensure depth of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3: Panel Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Review panel meets to discuss top-scoring applications; reviewers present orally and the panel assigns final scores after discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral presentation by assigned reviewers followed by panel discussion can alter preliminary scores; final scoring occurs post-discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of lay reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: AHA panels include lay reviewers (individuals without formal scientific training but with strong personal interest in heart disease/stroke prevention or management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay reviewers specifically evaluate the lay summary and score potential impact on the AHA mission; their integration formalizes public-impact assessment and is an unusual practice among major biomedical funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay-summary scoring / public-impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate scoring component assessing the lay summary and the potential impact of the proposal on AHA's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay-summary scoring is performed by lay reviewers to capture public-facing relevance and potential benefit; this complements scientific criteria by explicitly evaluating mission-aligned impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the research question to cardiovascular/stroke health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the proposed work addresses an important problem or critical barrier in heart disease or stroke research and its potential to advance the field or improve health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of the study design, methods, and analyses proposed to accomplish the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty of concepts or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether the project challenges current paradigms, introduces novel hypotheses, methods, technologies, or addresses previously unexplored areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the qualifications, track record, and suitability of the principal investigator(s) and key personnel to execute the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether institutional resources, facilities, and collaborators/mentors are adequate to support successful completion of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance of the proposal to heart disease and stroke and alignment with the AHA mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines how closely the proposed work supports the AHA's goals in preventing and treating cardiovascular disease and stroke; mission alignment is an explicit review criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predoctoral Fellowship review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to predoctoral fellowship applications (early-career training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations emphasize training potential, mentorship, career development, and suitability of the project to support trainee growth in cardiovascular research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Fellowship review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to postdoctoral fellowship applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors consider the candidate's training needs, mentorship environment, project feasibility for postdoctoral career development, and potential for independent research skills growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Award review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to career development awards aimed at early-career independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on evidence the award will transition the applicant toward independence, adequacy of mentorship and training plan, and feasibility of achieving independence milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Project Award review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to high-risk, innovative research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes novelty, potential high reward, feasibility given innovation risk, and whether the approach could substantially advance the field despite higher uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformational Project Award review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to paradigm-shifting, transformational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates potential for major shifts in current paradigms, scale of impact, and suitability of resources and team to pursue high-impact, long-term objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established Investigator Award review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to established investigator applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses sustained productivity, leadership, capacity to carry out larger or more complex projects, and continued contribution to cardiovascular research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategically Focused Research Networks review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Review criteria tailored to collaborative team awards (strategically focused networks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes team composition, collaborative structure, network-level aims, capacity for multi-site coordination, and potential for synergistic impact across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication: formalizing public-benefit criterion via lay review
rubrics_metrics.description: AHA's use of lay reviewers formalizes the 'public benefit' criterion by incorporating actual public participation in review rather than indirect proxies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinctive element should be considered when designing rubrics: include explicit public-impact assessment and mechanisms (e.g., lay summaries and lay scoring) to capture mission-relevant benefits.
